purpose: Freeze an isolated IQ2 in-model MTP on-versus-off experiment before canonical measurement.
hypotheses: MTP speedup will depend on workload-specific draft-token acceptance.
MTP will increase memory use because it activates the embedded NextN layer and a separate F16 draft cache.
Greedy MTP output should match MTP-off output; any mismatch will be reported rather than assumed away.

noncanonical_capability_probe.purpose: Confirm the pinned runtime actually activates the embedded MTP layer and discover its response timing fields before freezing canonical calculations.
startup_evidence: MTP draft context created against the target GGUF
16 MiB draft KV buffer and 31.50 MiB draft compute buffer
noncanonical_capability_probe.interpretation: Capability-only evidence; the prompt, seed, request length, and warmed state differ from the canonical protocol, so its speed is not a Phase 9 result.

measurement_order.limitation: Two workloads and a fixed counterbalanced order reduce neither workload-sampling uncertainty nor all time-order and thermal effects.

comparison_rules.primary_metric: mean server generation tokens per second within each workload
comparison_rules.output_equivalence: Compare SHA-256 of every retained greedy response between paired MTP states.
comparison_rules.relative_change_denominator: MTP off within the same workload

pre_measurement_gates.props_limitation: llama.cpp b10448 reports speculative.types as none in /props even while startup logs and response timing counters prove draft-mtp is active.

exit_condition: All four canonical records validate, MTP acceptance and output equivalence are derived from raw evidence, and conclusions remain bounded to the tested IQ2 runtime and two workloads.
